verdict.rationale: cubic documents an org-level `cubic-config` repository holding a `cubic.yaml`, which provides central review defaults. Each repo can also carry its own root `cubic.yaml` as the source of truth for review behavior, and role-based access controls who can change settings. The evidence does not say how org defaults and repo files take precedence, how exceptions are managed centrally, or that this works at the scale of hundreds of repos. Missing for 10: documented org-vs-repo inheritance and override precedence, centrally managed per-repo exceptions, evidence of rollout at scale, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering lead, I roll out org-level review defaults across hundreds of repos and manage exceptions centrally

citations.quote: Create a repository named `cubic-config` in your organization and add a `cubic.yaml` file to the root directory.
`cubic.yaml` lives in the root of your repository and becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents.
cubic uses a role-based access control system to manage who can make changes to your team's subscription and settings.
